verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own environments feature (dev, staging, production) lets flags be enabled or disabled per environment, and the toggle endpoint can switch flags in specific environments. A runtime probe confirmed a keyless local self-hosted instance can create and evaluate flags without an account, which gives an isolated test instance. However, environments scope flag state rather than isolating data; nothing documents a sandbox that separates experiment or warehouse data from production, and custom environments are a paid-tier feature. Missing for 10: documented data-isolated sandbox for experiments and metrics, explicit agent/MCP workflow targeting a non-production environment, independent corroboration of environment isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Use environments such as dev, staging, and production to enable or disable feature flags independently.
Feature flags can be enabled and disabled on a per-environment basis.
automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
a real flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license.
